new_individually_supported_fields.evidence: He names da on the eating root, specifies the changed final consonant, and explains why the alternative water-giving derivation would lose the required accent. He names dan for kunda on p. 163.
new_individually_supported_fields.alternate: PG187 also infers da from the accent of a jasmine word. Other lexica give dan for abda or kunda under other analyses. This new evidence applies to ad + da.

new_individually_supported_fields.evidence: He directly names tvan on the root and guṇa, followed by the word netvaḥ.
new_individually_supported_fields.alternate: The earlier assignment of dhyātva (thought) to tvan is still morphological. This word supplies an independent direct example for the field.

new_individually_supported_fields.evidence: The parent list spells knin. The local comment pairs the lū root with the short citation kniḥ. The following alternative vṛtti names lūniḥ from lunāti. The source spelling and the short technical citation together identify the fourth field.
new_individually_supported_fields.alternate: The rice meaning is supplied by Ujjvaladatta. This edition supplies affix evidence and the spelling without giving that gloss here.
